Mr. D.S. Gharsana For Respondent(s) : Mr. Mukhtiyar Khan, PP
Mr. Jayram Saran for complainant  HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE KULDEEP MATHUR
Order 13/05/2024 Corrected on 15.05.2024

By way of filing the present criminal misc. petition under Section 482 Cr.P.C., the petitioner has prayed for the following relief:-
"It is therefore most respectfully prayed that, the order passed by the learned Additional Session Judge Nokha, Bikaner dated 23-05-2023, in Criminal Revision No. 13/2023, CIS No. 6/2023) related to FIR No. 348/2022 P.S. Nokha, District Bikaner may kindly be set aside and the Misc. Petition filed by the petitioner may kindly be allowed and the Learned Judge may kindly be directed to released the said vehicle Leyland Model 3718 RC no. MH-43-BP-0338 and new RC no. RJ- 50-GA-4709,R.C and other documents of the petitioner, to hand over the petitioner."
[2024:RJ-JD:21248] (2 of 5)

] Briefly stated facts of the case are that the petitioner is the registered owner of the vehicle Leyland Model 3718 having registration No.
MH-43-BP-0338 (new Registration No. RJ-50-GA- 4709).
The petitioner executed an agreement to sale pertaining to the aforesaid vehicle in favour of respondent No.2.
As per the terms and conditions mentioned in the agreement to sale, the deal was finalized at a sum of Rs.24,00,000/-.

sentences.text: Respondent No.2 upon finalization of the deal, immediately paid Rs.4,00,000/- in cash and Rs.1,00,000/- were paid by transferring the amount in the account of the petitioner.

Further,
pursuant to the terms and conditions agreed to, between the parties, respondent No.2 gave 3 signed cheques bearing Nos. 816454, 816455, 816456 respectively (SBI Branch, Bhamatsar) of amount Rs.6,00,000/- each, to the petitioner.

As per the terms and conditions of the sale deed executed between the parties, the petitioner was first required to transfer the vehicle to respondent No.2 and thereupon, respondent No.2 was to clear the remaining amount, if any, within 10 days.

However, it was agreed between the parties that in case, respondent No.2 would fail to make full and final payment of the agreed amount, the vehicle would be transferred back, in the name of the petitioner.

It is to be noticed that on 14.02.2022, the present petitioner transferred the impugned vehicle in the name of respondent No.2, however, on his failure to fulfill the terms and conditions of the agreement to sale executed between the parties,
the vehicle was again got transferred in the name of the present [2024:RJ-JD:21248] (3 of 5)
[CRLMP-3550/2023] petitioner.
The petitioner is presently the registered owner of the vehicle in dispute.

Respondent No.2 being aggrieved by the action of the petitioner in getting the aforesaid vehicle re-transferred in his name, got an FIR No.348/2022, lodged at Police Station Nokha, District Bikaner against him for the offences punishable under Sections 420 and 406.
The vehicle in question was thereafter seized by the police during the course of investigation.

The petitioner as well as respondent No.2 filed applications before the learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Nokha, District Bikaner seeking release of the vehicle in question in their favour.

entities.text: Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Nokha, District Bikaner
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The learned trial Court after hearing the parties and on carefully considering their applications filed under Section 457 Cr.P.C., rejected the applications filed by both the parties vide order dated 17.01.2023 on the ground that the position with regard to the ownership over the vehicle was not clear and could be made clear only after investigation, therefore, the vehicle could not be released in favour of a particular party.
The petitioner as well as respondent No.2 being aggrieved by the order dated 17.01.2023 preferred revision petitions before the learned Additional Sessions Judge, Nokha, District Bikaner.

entities.text: Additional Sessions Judge, Nokha, District Bikaner
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Learned revisional Court after hearing the parties, vide impugned order dated 23.05.2023, while disposing of both the revision petitions, held that the vehicle in question was handed over to respondent No.2 on 14.03.2022, however, within the next 2 days i.e. on 16.03.2022, the same was again got registered in the name of the present petitioner, which is in violation of the terms [2024:RJ-JD:21248] (4 of 5)
[CRLMP-3550/2023] and conditions of the agreement to sale executed between the parties on 07.03.2022.
The learned revisional Court in the impugned order dated 23.05.2023, thus directed that the vehicle in question be released in favour of respondent No.2.
Heard learned counsel for the parties at Bar.
Perused the material available on record.
This Court has carefully perused the case file and the impugned order dated 23.05.2023 passed by the learned revisional Court.

sentences.text: In the opinion of this Court, the learned revisional Court was neither called upon to decide the question regarding the title of the vehicle in dispute nor the factum of violation of the terms and conditions of the agreement to sale deed entered between the parties.

The learned revisional Court was only required to decide as to who amongst the rival parties should be entrusted with the custody of the vehicle temporarily, till the learned trial Court passes the final order regarding disposal of the property on conclusion of the trial.

Ordinarily, when there is a dispute with regard to the title/ownership relating to any vehicle, the vehicle should be released in favour of the registered owner, till the dispute over the title is settled.

This is for the reason that the name of the registered owner is entered in the registration documents with the government authority, such as the Department of Motor Vehicle/Transport thereby making the individual or entity responsible for the vehicle and its legal obligations including payment of compensation etc., for the purposes of Motor Vehicles [2024:RJ-JD:21248] (5 of 5)
[CRLMP-3550/2023] Act.
However, to ensure that no damage is caused to the vehicle, the learned trial Court may impose certain conditions to ensure safety of the vehicle.
In view of the aforesaid discussion, the present misc. petition is allowed.

Respondent No.2 is directed to surrender the vehicle Leyland Model 3718 having registration No. MH-43-BP-0338 (new Registration No. RJ-50-GA-4709) before the learned trial Court within 10 days from the date of passing of this order.

The learned trial Court is directed to release the same in favour of the appellant by imposing the same conditions, on which the impugned vehicle was released in favour of respondent No.2 by the learned revisional Court.
All pending applications also stand disposed of.

(KULDEEP MATHUR),J 456-himanshu/-
